per_view_findings.finding: Candidate render has strong magenta/green false color, smeared terrain, and saturated diff coverage across the road and hillside boundary.
Boundary structure is present, but the render is not visually usable because the terrain is washed in purple/green noise and the heatmap is broadly saturated.
Road and hillside detail are heavily smeared with broad magenta cast; the visual mismatch is obvious despite metric gains in PSNR/SSIM.
Boundary panel keeps rough layout but loses natural color and fine detail; the diff panel is saturated across most terrain.
Horizon/terrain separation is unstable, with false cyan/magenta color and high diff response over the full landscape.
Mountain and foreground textures collapse into purple/black smear; horizon quality is worse than the reference and not production usable.
Long-range terrain and sky-adjacent areas show heavy magenta artifacts and texture smearing, matching the horizon metric regressions.
Horizon view has broad false-color artifacts and saturated difference heatmap, with visually obvious regression from the input frame.
Near-detail landscape is dominated by magenta/green false color and soft texture; the rendered detail would fail human inspection.
Road and lake context remain roughly aligned, but texture and color are heavily distorted and the diff map is nearly full-frame.
Candidate view shows dense purple/black texture noise and severe blur, consistent with the single-camera LPIPS regression.
Near-detail candidate is overrun by magenta false color and smeared terrain; it is not usable despite having nonblank render output.

recommended_next_action: Stop promotion and paid retries for this candidate. Do no-spend attribution on why the two-tile hard-output-cap merge improves boundary PSNR/SSIM but destroys color/perceptual quality, horizon, and near-detail structure before proposing another objective.

evidence.basis: Codex visual inspection of generated side-by-side panels after no-weights visual QA extraction, plus V18 comparison metrics.
